email.subject1: a signal play for dbt Labs
email.body1:
Nick, saw dbt Labs closed the Fivetran merger to build a unified data layer for AI.

A merger that big usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before reps can work them, and that is exactly where enterprise deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for dbt off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Nick, quick follow-up for dbt Labs.

Post-merger, the Northeast enterprise target usually climbs faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to cover the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your territory needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Nick, last bit of proof for dbt Labs.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how dbt's reply rate likely compares to peer data-infra teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Nick, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating a merger is its own kind of busy, and I get that timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your Northeast enterprise motion? I will tailor it to dbt either way.
